chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me; he said: A number of our companions narrated to me, among them Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-'Amriki ibn Ali, from Yahya (who was the servant of Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him)), from some of our companions, who traced it back to Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever visits me or visits any one of my progeny, I will visit him on the Day of Judgment and I will save him from its terrors.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet or his progeny according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes the intercessory power of the Prophet through the physical act of visiting his lineage, linking earthly devotion to eschatological salvation. It underscores the Shia concept of *Tawassul* (seeking means of approach), where the Prophet’s personal presence on Judgment Day serves as the ultimate deliverance from the *Awhal* (terrors) of the Hereafter.
